obligations.note: The change sets payments.privileged_idle_minutes and PRIVILEGED_IDLE_MINUTES to 16. SES-1 requires a privileged session idle more than 15 minutes to be rejected, and the catalog bound is payments.privileged_idle_minutes <= 15.
Ticket CHG-26996 is approved by change manager Grace Kim before review, and its components (payments.policy and payments.controls-data) cover policy.py and controls/payments/policy-params.json.
Sofia Santos, a payments change_approver and not the author Linh Nguyen, approved a code_review of the head commit.
The only commit is f72ea533703c316971e1a528bc1802641c1aab08, and both the code_review and control_owner approvals name that commit.

records/ci/run.json records a successful payments suite on the head commit, and the JUnit report includes the unskipped passing SES-1 control test test_privileged_idle_timeout_within_policy with 0 failures and 0 skipped.
The touched components payments.policy and payments.controls-data are not marked security_sensitive, so a security_review approval is not required.
controls/payments/policy-params.json is a protected path. Rachel Stein, a control_owner on the controls-office team (outside payments-eng), approved that role on the head commit.
The ticket type is standard and the change record sets emergency to false, so no post-implementation review is due.
The change relies on EXC-0184, which is approved and unexpired but scoped to mortgage.session, not payments. The payments SES-1 exception EXC-0141 expired on 2026-09-08, before review on 2026-10-08.
Acceptance-ledger covers are payments.py, audit.py, routes.py, and mortgage files. This change does not alter those paths, so prior evidence has not lapsed.

summary: The change raises Payments’s privileged idle limit from 15 minutes to 16 in both policy.py and policy-params.json, which violates SES-1. The cited exception EXC-0184 does not cure that deviation: it covers Mortgage sessions, and the Payments session exception EXC-0141 had already expired at review time. Ticket, independent approval, final-commit testing, and the control-owner approval for the protected policy file are in order, but the idle-timeout breach is not acceptable.
